subject: Minimum spend & overage smoothing for hosted API (Aurum Health)
messages:
From: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@aurumhealth.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@aurumhealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 17:23:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — question on minimums/overage smoothing

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the demo earlier — Aurum liked the latency profile and the prefix caching example. Before we move further with SRE and procurement, two quick pricing clarifications so we can scope the PO: 1) Our finance team prefers a small committed floor rather than a large upfront multi-month commit. Can you outline a minimum monthly commit you commonly accept for hosted customers and whether you offer pro-rated partial-months? 2) We have unpredictable surges tied to marketing campaigns. How do you price on-demand calls that exceed the commit within a billing month? Specifically: is there a smoothing/grace window where short bursts are averaged rather than billed at full on-demand overage rates?

If you have a one-page example (numbers) showing a $50k/mo baseline with two 72-hour spikes, that would help us. We may need ~30 days to get a PO, so an indicative structure for contract and overage would be great.

Appreciate it —
Lisa
Lisa Tran
VP Finance, Aurum Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — question on minimums/overage smoothing

Hi Lisa — great to hear Aurum liked the demo. See a proposed structure below (high level) and attached a simple spend model you can plug numbers into (Aurum_Initial_Spend_Model.xlsx).

Proposed commercial structure (hosted API):
- Minimum monthly commit: $25,000 (monthly recurring) — this is the minimum billable floor for the account.
- Overage (on-demand) rate: billed per-token at 1.8x the committed unit price for the remainder of the month once the commit is exhausted.
- Burst smoothing (grace window): 14-day smoothing window for transient spikes. If peak is resolved within 14 days and sustained monthly usage does not exceed the committed baseline by more than 25%, we offer an automatic credit equal to the difference between on-demand charges and a blended overage rate (effectively reducing the visible overage multiplier for short bursts).
- Sustained bursts: for sustained extra usage beyond the smoothing window (e.g., persistent >30% over baseline for more than 14 days) standard overage rate applies and we can discuss short-term temporary commit increases or a short-term top-up commit with preferential pricing.
- Volume discounts: tiered discounts on committed unit price at $100k, $250k, $500k yearly commit bands — details in the attached doc.

We typically allow a one-time pro-rata on-boarding invoice if customers sign mid-month; billing will be pro-rated to the calendar month.

Next steps: If that aligns, we can put the numbers into the attached DOC and share a redline-friendly term sheet + SLA excerpt (I attached Redwood_SLA_excerpt.pdf). If you want a lower overage multiplier for short bursts we can layer in surge credits tied to specific campaign windows.

Ben/Laura — looping you for pricing/legal polish.

Best,
Mateo
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — question on minimums/overage smoothing

Mateo — quick thoughts before we send final:
- 1.8x is safe but Aurum is large-healthcare and may push. Recommend offering 1.5x as an alternate, conditional on a 12-month minimum term (or a slightly higher $30k floor). That gives us protection and a competitive headline number.
- 14-day smoothing is ok; suggest adding an exception: if they can provide expected campaign windows (start/end dates) and we approve, we can treat approved campaign bursts as "approved transient spikes" and apply a reduced multiplier (1.25x) for that window up to a pre-agreed cap. This keeps our burst economics predictable.
- Add a clause re: abuse/automated test runs — spikes identified as non-production traffic are not eligible for smoothing credits.

I also suggest routing the final term sheet to Legal for two items: (1) clear definition of "smoothing window" and (2) calculation example for blended credits.

If you want, I can propose the alternative offer in-line when we reply to Lisa so they see both options (standard vs term-committed).

Ben Carter
Head of Sales, East | Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Tran <lisa.tran@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — question on minimums/overage smoothing

Hi Lisa — thanks for the thoughtful questions and for running this through Finance. To summarize and give you two concrete paths so procurement can move quickly:

Option A (Flex monthly, shorter term):
- $25k minimum monthly commit
- On-demand overage multiplier: 1.8x committed unit price
- 14-day smoothing window with automatic credits for transient spikes (see attached model)
- No upfront annual commitment required (month-to-month)

Option B (12 month term, preferential overage):
- $30k minimum monthly commit (12-month term)
- On-demand overage multiplier: 1.5x committed unit price
- Approved campaign windows can receive a temporary reduced multiplier of 1.25x up to an agreed cap

Attachments: I attached a short offer doc (20270802-Aurum-Commit-Offer.docx) and an SLA excerpt we referenced. If you like Option B we can issue a redline-ready term sheet and send a DocuSign for the PO/contract path. Otherwise, Option A keeps you flexible while still giving smoothing protections for short bursts.

Requested next steps from Aurum: 1) indicate preferred option (A or B), 2) share any planned campaign windows or expected burst dates (if you want to petition for approved-campaign pricing), and 3) confirm procurement timeline so we can align invoicing/pro-rata schedule.

If it's helpful I can schedule a quick 30-min call this week to walk the procurement and SRE teams through the spend model.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
VP Commercial | Redwood Inference
